items.summary: Recommendation: maintain the existing evidence-needed security disposition. Fleet-doctor and operations sweeps have no results, so authentication, secrets, isolation, release, dependency, monitoring, incident, TLS, and disclosure controls remain unverified. Continue bounded read-only evidence work; no public exposure or security-sensitive release is supported.

Security disposition: evidence_needed for fleet-wide clearance; blocked for public exposure and security-sensitive releases; conditional for ordinary reversible growth. Exact decision: preserve private launch gates and permit only bounded reversible work that adds no credentials, permissions, dependencies, data collection, cross-site behavior, or security-sensitive exposure. Evidence: fleet-doctor has no run or control results; operations deploy-health, uptime, and error sweeps have no results; authentication and access boundaries, secrets handling, container isolation, release approvals and provenance, dependency controls, data exposure, monitoring, incident response, complete TLS posture, and security.txt/disclosure readiness remain unverified. No certificates are reported expiring within 30 days, but that does not establish complete TLS coverage. Compliance is technical-only with 37 pass, 15 fail, and 7 unknown; analytics data quality is yellow. Existing failed requests and 47 open failure follow-ups are containment signals, not proof of exploitation. Do not claim certification or a clean bill of health. Continue the existing bounded read-only security evidence matrix using authorized metadata and retained artifacts only; do not access credentials or private containers, change permissions or configuration, add dependencies, deploy, requeue failures, or conduct external outreach.

Retain the existing security evidence work and do not create duplicate requests or production work. Record dated, redacted evidence, affected scope, owners, explicit unknowns, severity, and release implications for authentication and access boundaries, secrets exposure, runtime isolation, release controls, dependency provenance, TLS, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and disclosure readiness.
